cls: First-generation antihistamine - propylamine (alkylamine) class H1-receptor antagonist
quick: 4 mg every 4-6 hours (max 24 mg/24 h). Extended-release: 8-12 mg every 8-12 hours
May be taken with or without food; take with food or water if it upsets the stomach
Generally considered acceptable; one of the antihistamines with longest safety record
Small amounts in milk; may reduce milk supply and cause infant irritability/drowsiness - use lowest dose
Use with caution; reduce dose/frequency in significant impairment
Use with caution in hepatic impairment
Avoid - marked additive sedation and CNS depression
Sedation, anticholinergic effects; caution in elderly
summary: Chlorpheniramine maleate is a first-generation (sedating) antihistamine of the propylamine/alkylamine class that blocks H1 receptors and has anticholinergic and sedative activity. It relieves symptoms of allergic rhinitis (hay fever), upper respiratory allergies, urticaria, and is a common component of cold/cough combination products. It causes drowsiness, dry mouth, and other anticholinergic effects, so caution is needed in the elderly and in glaucoma, prostatic enlargement, and respiratory disease.
indications: Temporary relief of allergic rhinitis (hay fever) symptoms: sneezing, runny nose, itching of the nose or throat, and itchy/watery eyes
Symptomatic relief of other upper respiratory allergies and the common cold (often in combination products)
Symptomatic treatment of urticaria and allergic skin reactions/pruritus

dosage.n: Do not exceed 24 mg (6 tablets) in 24 hours
Max 12 mg/24 h; under 6 years consult a doctor

dosage.d: Use only as directed by a doctor

admin: May be taken with or without food; take with water or food if it causes stomach upset
Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not crush or chew
Take a dose at bedtime if daytime drowsiness is a problem
Do not exceed the maximum daily dose; avoid duplicate antihistamines in combination cold products
Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you
moa: Chlorpheniramine is a propylamine-derivative (alkylamine) antihistamine that acts as a competitive H1-receptor antagonist, preventing released histamine from dilating capillaries and causing edema of the respiratory mucosa, and from producing itch/wheal responses. It also possesses anticholinergic and central sedative activity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to chlorpheniramine or other alkylamine antihistamines
Use in nursing mothers (per traditional labeling, due to risk to the infant)
relative: Symptomatic prostatic hyperplasia / bladder-neck obstruction / urinary retention
Stenosing peptic ulcer or pyloroduodenal obstruction
monitor: Anticholinergic effects (urinary retention, constipation, dry mouth)

preg: Chlorpheniramine has one of the longest safety records among antihistamines and is generally considered acceptable for use in pregnancy when needed. Human data have not demonstrated a clear increase in malformations. Use the lowest effective dose and avoid near term if possible.
lact: Small amounts are excreted into breast milk. First-generation antihistamines may reduce milk supply (especially with decongestants) and can cause irritability or drowsiness in the nursing infant. Use the lowest effective dose; non-sedating alternatives may be preferred during breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution; consider reduced dose or extended interval in significant renal impairment, as the drug and metabolites are renally eliminated.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; chlorpheniramine is extensively hepatically metabolized and clearance may be reduced.

major: MAO inhibitors (prolong and intensify anticholinergic effects - avoid)
moderate: Alcohol and other CNS depressants (sedatives, hypnotics, opioids, benzodiazepines) - additive sedation/CNS depression
Other anticholinergic drugs (additive dry mouth, urinary retention, confusion)
minor: Tricyclic antidepressants (additive anticholinergic and sedative effects)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - marked additive sedation and CNS depression
interactions.diagnostics: May suppress skin-test (allergy) reactions - withhold for several days before allergy skin testing

serious: Confusion or excitation (especially in elderly or children)
emergency: Anticholinergic toxidrome with hyperthermia and arrhythmia (overdose)

monitoring: Degree of sedation and ability to perform tasks safely
Anticholinergic effects (urinary retention, constipation, confusion), especially in elderly
Symptom relief and avoidance of overdose / duplicate antihistamines
Intraocular pressure in patients with glaucoma
counsel: This medicine commonly causes drowsiness - do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you
Avoid alcohol and other sedating medicines while taking it
It can cause dry mouth, constipation, and difficulty urinating; report trouble passing urine or eye pain
Do not take with other products containing antihistamines, and do not exceed the labeled dose
Use cautiously in older adults and keep out of reach of children (overdose can be dangerous)
pk: Antihistaminic effect within 15 to 60 minutes of an oral dose
Plasma peak approximately 2 to 6 hours after an oral dose
Approximately 20 to 24 hours in adults (longer than many other antihistamines)
Symptom relief approximately 4 to 6 hours (immediate-release); longer for extended-release
Store at controlled room temperature, 20-25 C; protect from moisture and light
pearls: Classic sedating (first-generation) antihistamine - causes drowsiness and anticholinergic effects; non-sedating agents are preferred for daytime/long-term allergy control
Listed on Beers Criteria as potentially inappropriate in the elderly due to anticholinergic burden
Has a long half-life (~20-24 h) despite its short symptomatic effect, allowing extended-release formulations
Frequently combined with decongestants/analgesics/antitussives in cold preparations - watch for duplicate antihistamine dosing
missed: If taking it on a schedule, take the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double up. For as-needed allergy use, simply take a dose when symptoms occur, observing the maximum daily limit.
overdose: Overdose can cause CNS depression (sedation, coma) or, especially in children, paradoxical CNS stimulation (excitation, hallucinations, seizures) plus a marked anticholinergic toxidrome (fixed dilated pupils, flushing, dry mucous membranes, hyperthermia, tachycardia, urinary retention). Management is supportive: protect the airway, control seizures, treat hyperthermia, and provide symptomatic/supportive care; activated charcoal may be considered for recent large ingestions.
